summary:
The core of the design is sound and checks out against the code. The Fact's body matches what spike 1 ran. All five regexes in the repro accept the planned text. TopLevelTracker's Seed/Moved/Build branches behave as the design says. Placing the Fact in TopLevelTests is right, and the Microsoft Learn source supports the NTFS per-name staleness the Fact relies on. Three things need fixing, all in how the guard is verified rather than in the guard itself:

- **(M1, major)** The mutant-A kill check, which is how C2 gets settled at build and at validate, exists only as a prose procedure. Nothing is committed. That breaks accepted check CC-004 and reinterprets lesson #428 ("apply mutants only through Mutants.ps1"). The prose has also already lost guards that Mutants.ps1 enforces in code.
- **(m1)** That same procedure never sweeps up copies left by killed runs (CC-009). Its "let eng/dotnet.ps1 bootstrap" option downloads an SDK of about 300 MB into every copy.
- **(m2)** The order of the asserts defeats the stated reason for the snapshot-0 assertion. If the directory entry has already been refreshed, the flags assert fails first, not snapshot 0 as the contract's error case claims.

findings.claim: C2's only proof is the case 'the guard dies with the defect it guards', and its check is a multi-step procedure written in prose: copy the worktree, hash src, hand-edit TopLevelTracker.cs in the copy, run a filtered test, stop VBCSCompiler, delete the copy, check git diff. Nothing is committed. Build has to run it and so does validate. This is exactly what accepted check CC-004 forbids: a case obligation resting on an uncommitted throwaway probe instead of a committed, runnable command. It also reinterprets lesson #428, whose text is 'Hand-written mutation scripts corrupted the real worktree once. Apply mutants only through Mutants.ps1', as 'honoured by never mutating the worktree'. The design says it follows Mutants.ps1's safety discipline, but every step of that discipline is now kept by memory, and the prose has already drifted from the script it cites. It drops three guards Mutants.ps1 enforces in code: Old text must match exactly once, the build is --no-incremental with FsAnalyser.Core.dll written after the edit or the run is void, and a mutant run that executes a different number of tests than the baseline is void. It also does not leave .taad/slices and .taad-scratch out of the copy. The stale-build trap is not hypothetical: spike 2 recorded 'A first baseline attempt was invalid: MSBuild did not rebuild, and it still showed 936'. The engine also cannot register a prose check as a runnable case, so validate either rebuilds the script by hand (the #428 failure mode) or halts on an uncovered case (#331).
findings.evidence: Design, component 'Mutant-A kill verification': 'No script is committed, and SL-102's Mutants.ps1 roster is not edited'. Case 'the guard dies with the defect it guards', check text. CC-004. Lesson #428. tests/bugs/SL-102-LastAccessGatesAssertions/Mutants.ps1:19-24 lists the guards the prose omits.

quote.text: - each mutant's old text must match exactly once, the build is --no-incremental, and the test build's FsAnalyser.Core.dll must

findings.fix: Commit the check as a runnable script in the slice's own folder, for example tests/bugs/SL-105-FileRowRevisedGuard/Mutants.ps1. Model it on SL-102's script: the same copy step via git ls-files without .taad/slices and .taad-scratch, the target refused if it resolves under the worktree, Old matched exactly once, --no-incremental plus a check that the Core.dll was written after the edit, DOTNET_ROOT pointed at the worktree's .dotnet, and a src hash plus `git diff --exit-code -- src` at the end. It runs only the TopLevel filter and expects exactly {TopLevelTests.AnInPlaceCorrectionOfARootLevelFileNameMarksThatFileRowRevised} red, with the 'row a-stale.bin: Revised is False' message. Name that one command as the case's check, allocated to build-slice. SL-102's ValidateSet and its 'All' stay untouched, which still meets the design's concern about the roster.

findings.claim: The mutant procedure creates %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-sl105-mutant-<guid>, a whole-repo copy (spike 1 copied 6,604 files), and its only cleanup is a step at the end. Nothing sweeps copies left by a killed run, as accepted check CC-009 requires. A killed run is the expected path here, not an edge case: the engine's case runner kills at 120 s (Q-222, repro.py:63), tool calls have their own limits (Q-132), and spike 1's own cleanup first failed because VBCSCompiler held the copy's SDK files. The procedure also allows 'plus .dotnet or let eng/dotnet.ps1 bootstrap'. Bootstrapping downloads about 300 MB of SDK into each copy (#72), while Mutants.ps1 deliberately avoids that.
findings.evidence: Design case check: 'Copy the worktree (git ls-files -co --exclude-standard, plus .dotnet or let eng/dotnet.ps1 bootstrap) into a new %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-sl105-mutant-<guid>'. CC-009. Q-222. Lesson #72. Spike 1's note on VBCSCompiler holding .dotnet\sdk.

quote.text: .dotnet/ that eng/dotnet.ps1 installs (it is used through DOTNET_ROOT and PATH, so the copy downloads nothing).

findings.fix: In the committed script from M1, start by sweeping %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp\fsa-sl105-mutant-* left by earlier runs, after `build-server shutdown` for each. Use the worktree's .dotnet through DOTNET_ROOT and PATH instead of copying or bootstrapping it.
findings.class_of: scratch roots leaked when a run is killed

findings.claim: The design adds the snapshot-0 assertion so that a refreshed directory entry 'fails at a line that names the cause'. The contract's error case says 'A refreshed directory entry fails at the snapshot-0 assertion (64 MiB, not 1 MiB)'. With the stated order, that does not happen. If the entry was refreshed before Seed, the probe reads the same size as the listing. Probes is still 1 (_probes++ runs before the comparison), but ProbeCorrected is never set. Watch's AssertSnapshotsHold passes, because nothing moved and correctedRows only permits change. Assertion (2) passes, and assertion (3) `Store.Flags(stale) == SizeProbed | ProbeCorrected` fails first, reporting the flags rather than the stale fixture. The snapshot-0 assertion (4) is never reached.
findings.evidence: Design component 'Root-level stale-hardlink File-row Fact', 'Asserts, in order: (1) … (2) Probes == 1. (3) … Store.Flags(stale) == SizeProbed | ProbeCorrected. (4) Named(scan.Snapshots[0], …)'. Key decision 'Assert the stale precondition explicitly'. Contract error_cases. Scanner.cs:517-524.
findings.fix: Move the snapshot-0 assertion (4) to directly after the Completed assertion and before the Probes and flags assertions, so that a refreshed fixture fails at the line that names it, as the rationale and the contract say.

dimensions_checked.result: The must-verify precondition, that NTFS per-name staleness also holds on Windows 10, was checked on the web. Microsoft Learn's 'Hard Links and Junctions' says 'the directory entry size and attribute information of the file are visibly updated only at the link through which the change was made' (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/fileio/hard-links-and-junctions), and the 2018 MSDN archive (web.archive.org/web/20180619181640/…aa365006) says the same. The source documents it as NTFS behaviour with no version qualifier, so the recalled prior-art claim is accurate. If it were false on Windows 10, the Fact would fail loudly on correct code there, at the flags assert (see m2). The existing folder-row Fact AnInPlaceCorrectionOfAnEarlierNameIsCreditedToThatNamesRow already depends on the same staleness, so the slice adds no new platform exposure. Q-249's catalog re-run is recalled, but the design does not lean on it: the Fact in the default suite is the standing guard.

None material. Root listing order is irrelevant because the root listing commits before sub is descended, so a-stale.bin is always the name seen first and probed (Probes == 1 was measured). TempTree.Hardlink and Append (TempTree.cs:173-177, 279-283) touch only the sub name after the link exists, so nothing refreshes a-stale.bin. A concurrent opener such as Defender or another test is the same exposure the sibling folder-row Fact has had since SL-063, and spike 2 measured 63 of 63 runs stale. The link and uncorrected-file rows are correctly marked not material: Build never makes a Link row Done (TopLevelTracker.cs:188).

The mutant-kill verification is kept by memory, not built into a script (M1), and it has no orphan sweep (m1). The Fact itself enforces its own fixture rule by construction: any pre-scan open of a-stale.bin makes it fail.

None. One Fact of about 30 lines, the repro committed unchanged, no src change, no new helper. Re-running the kill at build and validate is justified because the committed Fact text may differ from spike 1's.

The contract's error case for a refreshed entry names the wrong failing line (m2). The other error cases match the code: the watcher's message under mutant A was measured, and sub's `(corrected || !row.Revised)` holds for any wrong-row credit.
None. A mklink failure throws from TempTree.Run and is never skipped (Q-001). A refreshed fixture cannot pass vacuously: the final literal-true Revised assertion and the flags assertion both fail.

None from the brief, the investigation's fix direction or spike 1's diff. The Fact body, its placement and its assertion list match all three. The taste choice of TopLevelTests over HardlinkTests is correct: Watch, Put, Named and Watched are private (TopLevelTests.cs:560-597, 738, 744).

CC-004 and #428 are broken by the prose-only mutant check (M1), and CC-009 by the missing sweep (m1). CC-008 holds. The repro csproj has no SMBLibrary reference or pin redefinition, so SmbLibraryPinTests.cs:29-45 stays green. It has no DllImport, so InteropLivesOnlyInNative (tests) holds. Its wording does not trip RigLockScopeWordingTests. SL-102's source reader is monotonic (units.Any), so adding a unit cannot turn it red. bin/ and obj/ are gitignored, so committing the folder leaves them out. Q-114 does not apply, because no TopLevel*.cs file changes.

Adequate. The Fact also reaches Moved's root-child exit (TopLevelTracker.cs:119-121), which no existing test reaches: every existing Move is on a depth-2 record (HandDriven a\a.bin, 1-folder\stale.bin). The repro's regexes were checked against the planned text: RootLevelHardlink, GrowsTheFile, ScansARealTree, FileRow, and AssertsRevisedTrue via the literal true in an Assert.Equal tuple. The trailing [Fact] unit that swallows the helpers has no Hardlink(, so it cannot satisfy the reader falsely.

None. The slice is test-only: a temp tree under %TEMP%\fsa-tests via TempTree, cmd.exe mklink /H as already used by HardlinkTests, no elevation, no network, no registry, and the repro project writes nothing.
